chunks: The Shaykh, the jurist, Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us. He said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us. He said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ubaydillah narrated to me, from his father, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them all) who said:
The masters of the people in this world are the generous, and in the Hereafter are the pious.

key_terms.الأتقياء: The pious ones — plural of taqi, denoting taqwa (God-consciousness and piety)
key_terms.الأسخياء: The generous ones — plural of sakhi, denoting open-handedness and liberality
key_terms.سادة: Masters, leaders, chiefs — plural of sayyid, denoting those who hold authority and eminence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about who are the true masters among people?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) draws a profound contrast between the qualities that earn leadership in this world versus the next. In the worldly realm, generosity and open-handedness elevate a person to a position of social leadership, as the generous attract followers and earn respect. However, in the afterlife, it is piety (taqwa) and God-consciousness that determine true mastery and honor before God. This teaching, transmitted through the lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt via Zayd ibn Ali, was delivered in one of Shaykh al-Saduq's Friday assemblies in Sha'ban 367 AH to his students in Nishapur.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
